sources.entry: MacSweep - Free, open-source Mac cleaner written in Rust (~7 MB) for junk cleanup, large files, app uninstalling with leftovers and orphaned launch agents, with tests ensuring browser profiles, Mail and app data are never deleted. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/nihal4/macsweep) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: MacSweep is a free, open-source Mac cleaner written in Rust that removes junk files, finds large old files, fully uninstalls apps including leftovers, and removes orphaned launch agents.
keywords: open source alternative to paid mac cleaners
summary.what_it_does: MacSweep is a native macOS app that scans for caches, logs, build leftovers and Trash, and shows a per-category summary before cleaning, with per-file checkboxes. It lists large files in the home folder grouped by kind, with a filter for files not opened in a year. The Uninstaller shows each app's size including leftovers and separates leftovers into a safe-to-remove group and a "Your data" group that is not pre-selected. The Launch Agents view lists background helpers and flags those whose app is already gone. The sidebar shows free disk space and Trash size and offers an Empty Trash button. The README states that it has no network access, no telemetry and no accounts.
use_cases: free up disk space on a Mac
completely uninstall a Mac app with its leftovers
clean developer caches such as Xcode and npm
how_to_run: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf | sh (one-time Rust install, per README)
./scripts/setup-signing.sh (optional, keeps Full Disk Access across rebuilds)
UNIVERSAL=1 ./bundle.sh (Apple Silicon and Intel in one app)
notable: Allowlist-based deletion: junk cleaning only deletes inside fixed cache, log and build folders, and each path is rechecked before deletion
Uninstaller keeps user data such as browser profiles, containers and cookies unless explicitly selected
Automated tests (cargo test) check that browser profiles, Mail, keychains and Documents cannot be deleted
Apps, large files and launch agents go to the Trash so Put Back works; only junk is deleted permanently
Small ~7 MB binary with no web view
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so first launch needs right-click Open or removing the quarantine attribute
Requires granting Full Disk Access and Finder control permissions for full functionality
Roadmap items such as duplicate finder, scheduled scans, Homebrew install and notarized builds are not yet implemented
Browser cache cleanup per browser is listed as a roadmap item only
